summary: Claros Learn (LMS) — Phase 36. Tested backend RBAC, student flows (enrollments, content, assignment submission, quiz attempt, progress), faculty flows (course listing, content section, AI quiz generation, AI grading) and frontend testids on /learn, /learn/courses/:id, /learn/faculty/:id. 13/13 backend tests pass. UI selectors all resolve. AI integrations (Claude via Emergent LLM) returned real responses — quiz generated 5 questions in ~25s, AI grade returned a coherent score+feedback.

minor.issue: Course payload exposes faculty_user_id; harmless but consider stripping for students.

After student has attempted, correct_option is included on the GET — fine for results, but the same endpoint is reused for the player. Behavior is documented in code (hide pre-attempt only) so OK; flagging only for completeness.

action_items: Assignment rows in the Assignments tab use data-testid prefix 'learn-assignment-row-' (not 'learn-content-row-' as worded in the request). Implementation matches code in ClarosLearnCourse.jsx — no fix needed, but main agent may want to keep this in mind when updating tests/docs.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_learn.py — _ensure_course_access allows ANY hod/dean to grade/manage ANY course in the tenant (regardless of department). For a multi-department institution this may over-permission; consider scoping HOD by department_id.
routes_learn.py — submit_attempt returns 200 with score, but does NOT include attempt_id in the body field expected by the UI's results URL pattern — it does return 'attempt_id' though, so OK.

routes_learn.py — _recompute_progress double-counts: it counts ALL submissions+attempts for the student across the tenant, then clamps to total. The clamp hides cross-course inflation but progress numbers may still be misleading once the student has many courses.

routes_learn.py — File download endpoint reconstructs disk path as {iid}_{token}, but the upload also prepends {iid}_, leading to safe behavior; consider hashing path so files can't be guessed by predicting fid+filename.

routes_learn.py — _safe_json uses depth counter but increments depth on EVERY char equal to start char including the very first one — correct, but if JSON contains escaped quotes/braces in strings, this naive parser may mis-balance. Acceptable for LLM output.

The student's quiz attempt is idempotent (test handles both first-attempt and already-attempted states). Faculty AI quiz generation hits real Claude — allow up to 120s. HOD has tenant-wide access, used for AI grading test since prof.suresh's courses may not overlap with the student's enrolled set (round-robin assignment).
